name: Open Logic Project
goodFor: An open text on propositional and first-order logic, sets, relations and computability for philosophy, mathematics and CS.

The Open Logic Project is an open source, open access collection of materials on advanced logic, aimed mainly at philosophers, but also suitable for computer scientists and mathematicians.
This repository contains LaTeX source files only.

notes: The project's own GitHub repository README declares The Open Logic Text CC BY 4.0 ("Author(s): The Open Logic Project"), and LICENSE.md holds the CC BY 4.0 legal code, which allows commercial use, so a paid app may show a passage with the credit in attribution; nothing read limits commercial or automated use. The licence statement read is the repository's, not the project website's: openlogicproject.org and builds.openlogicproject.org were not reachable and not read, so any site terms are unchecked. The repository holds LaTeX source only, so text shown would come from a PDF build of that source. The README describes the material as advanced logic aimed mainly at philosophers; the propositional and first-order logic, sets, relations and functions parts suit an introductory logic or discrete mathematics course, while the metalogic, computability and incompleteness parts are beyond lower division.
